preparations.name: Square groove
preparations.description: Square edges with a root opening and no machining. For thin material, roughly up to 1/4 in (6 mm) welded from one side; the welding procedure sets the limit.

preparations.name: Single-V groove
preparations.description: Both edges beveled (here 30° each, a 60° groove angle) above a small root face. The common prep for plate and pipe from about 1/4 in up; pipe bevels are often 37.5° per side.

preparations.name: Single-bevel groove
preparations.description: Only one edge is beveled (here 45°). Used when only one piece can be cut, as on the upright plate of a T-joint.

preparations.name: J-groove
preparations.description: One edge cut to a curved J. It needs less weld metal than a bevel on thick plate, but costs more to machine.

preparations.name: U-groove
preparations.description: Both edges cut to a J, making a U. The least filler on very thick sections, and the most machining.

letters: f = root face, or land (the flat at the bottom of a bevel)
α = groove angle, between the two bevels
β = bevel angle of one edge
